To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ceramide is excluded from transition vesicles and cell-free transfer via vesicles and, therefore, is transferred by a non-vesicular, ATP- and cytosol-independent mechanism.

cell-free transfer of phospholipids and glycolipids from endoplamic reticulum to the Golgi complex occurs by two distinct mechanisms: (1) via vesicular intermediates that are temperature-dependent, ATP-dependent, and cytosol-dependent; (2) via a non-vesiclar mechanism that is temperature-dependent but neither ATP- nor N-ethylmaleimid-dependent.
the cell-free transfer of phosphatidylethanolamine from endoplasmatic reticulum to golgi apparatus is mediated by transition vesicles and is temperature-, ATP- but not N-ethylmaleimid-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of transfer of lipids, particularly phospholipids, between the endoplasmic-reticulum-Golgi system and the plasma membrane of mammalian cells.
the cell-free transfer of lipid from endoplasmatic reticulum to the Golgi.
the mechanism of cell-free transfer of lipid between organelles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lipid sorting observed in the present work is not a result of lipid sorting during vesicle formation, but is a result of the mechanism of transfer of lipid from transitional endoplamic reticulum to the Golgi complex.
the cell-free transfer of sphingolipids from endoplamic reticulum to the Golgi is mediated by vesicles and is temperature-, ATP-, cytosol-dependent and inhibited by sulfhydryl-blocking agents.

the cell-free transfer of phosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidylserine from endoplasmatic reticulum to transitional endoplasmatic and transition vesicles is temperature-dependent and ATP- and NEM-dependent.
